To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Training affine transformations of features in a deep network is surprisingly powerful; (2) This power is in part due to BatchNorm learning to disable a significant fraction of the randomly initialized features; (3) Training only the affine transformations of features leads to surprisingly high classification performance; (4) This high performance can be achieved even when training the affine transformations of only a small fraction of the features; and (5) The high performance achieved when training the affine parameters alone

training only BatchNorm's learned affine transforms in a ResNet can achieve 82% accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 32% accuracy on ImageNet, and that BatchNorm achieves this in part by learning to disable around one-third of random features.

(1) training BatchNorm and Only BN (training affine parameters and freezing all other weights in a CNN) achieves high performance on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet and (2) the performance of Only BN is significantly higher than that of a random network of similar size, which is a consequence of the network learning to disable a large fraction of random features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
answering the question: how much can you achieve by training only the affine parameters of random features?
the role of affine transformations of random features, and we hope that the insights gained from this work will help to better understand and design deep learning architectures.

the following questions: (1) How much can we learn about a neural network's performance by only training its affine parameters, without learning the features they transform? (2) How much can a neural network learn about the data from random features, without learning the parameters that shift and rescale them?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
affine parameters in BatchNorm are not only expressive but they can be very expressive.

“The expressive power of neural nets is not only determined by the weights of the network, but also the affine transformations that the network performs.” This is an important result that has implications in many different areas of machine learning.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expressive power of random features is surprisingly high.
the expressive power of a deep neural network is largely determined by the random features it uses, not by the architecture that it uses.
the random features are not random at all, and that the expressive power of a neural network is not just the number of parameters, but also the way in which they are used.
The main takeaway from our work is that

random features in deep networks are not just a convenient initialization scheme, but can actually be used to learn powerful representations in their own right, and in a way that is complementary to the learning of more traditional, non-random representations.
random features are more powerful than previously thought, and that BatchNorm is a powerful way to leverage that expressive power.
